tagline: Japan's first great capital, where sacred deer roam free beneath UNESCO temples and the Great Buddha.

taxi.color: varies by company (often green, black, or livery-branded)
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with a base fare around ¥500-700 (~$3-4) for the first 1-2km; readily found at both JR Nara and Kintetsu Nara stations, less common to hail on the street elsewhere.

emergency.note: Japan has no single unified emergency number; 110 reaches police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance services.

hood_desc: Home to Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall, Kasuga Taisha, and the free-roaming sacred deer of Nara Park; the essential first stop for temple-hopping, best for first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.

A beautifully preserved Edo- and Meiji-era merchant quarter of narrow lanes, wooden townhouses, cafes, and craft shops just south of Nara Park; suits travelers who want a boutique, photogenic base with local character.

The modern transport hub around JR Nara Station with department stores, chain hotels, and easy rail access to Kyoto and Osaka; practical for travelers prioritizing transit convenience and reliable business hotels.

A lively shopping street connecting Kintetsu Nara Station to Nara Park, lined with souvenir shops, restaurants, and arcades; good for travelers who want to be steps from both a station and the sights.

A quiet, leafy residential area near Yoshiki-en and Isuien gardens on the eastern edge of Nara Park, home to the historic Nara Hotel; suits travelers wanting a calmer, more local-feeling stay away from the crowds.
lodging: Shisui, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Nara
Super Hotel JR Nara Ekimae Sanjo Dori
Super Hotel Premier JR Nara Eki

transit.hours: Buses and trains run roughly 5:30 AM to midnight; no late-night rail or bus service.
transit.pay: IC cards (ICOCA, Suica, Pasmo, etc.) are widely accepted on buses and trains; cash also works on buses.
transit.note: Central Nara (Nara Park, Naramachi, both stations) is compact and highly walkable; buses are mainly useful for outlying temples like Horyu-ji.

transit.m: JR/Kintetsu limited express with transfer via Osaka or Tsuruhashi (~75-90 min)
Airport limousine bus to Nara (~90 min, limited schedule)

tip.r: Tipping is not practiced in Japan; attempting to tip at restaurants or with taxi drivers is unnecessary and can cause confusion.

tagline: Guangdong's inkstone capital, where karst peaks rise from Star Lake beside a Ming Dynasty city wall.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with a base fare around ¥8-10 for the first 2-3km; the DiDi app is more convenient than street-hailing for non-Chinese speakers and lets you set a destination in advance.

emergency.note: China does not use a single unified emergency number; 110 reaches police, 120 reaches ambulance services, and 119 reaches fire.

hoods: Star Lake / Seven Star Crags Area
hood_desc: The scenic core of Zhaoqing around Star Lake and the Seven Star Crags, an AAAAA-rated karst-peak park often compared to Guilin; best for travelers who want the city's signature natural landmark right outside their hotel.
The historic quarter in and around Zhaoqing's Ming Dynasty city wall, with the Chongxi Pagoda, old temples, and traditional streets; suits travelers wanting a slower-paced, heritage-focused base.
The commercial heart of Duanzhou District along Tianning Road, with malls, restaurants, and everyday city life; practical for travelers who want easy transit and shopping access.

A green, spread-out district built around Dinghu Mountain, China's first nature reserve, with hot springs and forest trails; ideal for travelers prioritizing nature and relaxation over sightseeing density.

A quieter northern residential district away from the main tourist core, offering a more local, lower-key look at everyday Zhaoqing; suited to travelers who prefer calm surroundings with easy bus access downtown.
lodging: Hanting Hotel Zhaoqing Qixingyan East Gate
7 Days Inn Zhaoqing Qixing Memorial Arch
Hanting Hotel Zhaoqing Qixingyan East Gate

transit.hours: City buses generally run about 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; no metro or dedicated night bus network.
transit.pay: Fares (¥2-4) are paid in cash on board or via mobile QR code (Alipay/WeChat Pay); no dedicated rechargeable transit card is required for visitors.
transit.note: Zhaoqing has no metro; buses, DiDi ride-hailing, and taxis cover the city, while the Guangzhou-Zhaoqing Intercity Railway and Zhaoqing East high-speed rail station connect to the wider Greater Bay Area.

air: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (nearest major hub, ~110km)
bus: Intercity coaches to Guangzhou, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong

car.idp: Not recognized; a Chinese driver's license or certified translation is required

transit.m: Intercity coach from Baiyun Airport to Zhaoqing (~2 hrs)
Airport shuttle plus Guangzhou-Zhaoqing Intercity Railway (~2 hrs total)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is not expected at restaurants, taxis, or hotels.

tagline: Alpine city of Zenko-ji pilgrims, 1998 Olympic legacy, and gateway to the Japanese Alps.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with a base fare around ¥700-800 (~$4-5); readily available at Nagano Station taxi stands, though less common to hail on the street outside downtown.

emergency.note: Japan has no single unified emergency number; 110 reaches police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance services.

hood_desc: The modern hub around JR/Shinkansen Nagano Station with department stores, chain hotels, and the Zenkoji-guchi exit leading straight toward the temple; best for travelers prioritizing easy Shinkansen access and reliable business hotels.

The atmospheric pilgrim approach to Zenko-ji, one of Japan's most important Buddhist temples, lined with the Nakamise shopping street's traditional shops, soba restaurants, and temple lodgings; suits travelers who want to be steps from the city's spiritual heart.

Nagano's historic covered shopping arcade and downtown core linking the station to Zenko-ji, packed with local eateries, izakaya, and everyday shops; good for travelers who want a walkable, lived-in city-center base.

A preserved former castle town on the city's edge with samurai residences, earthen storehouses, and the ruins of Matsushiro Castle; suits travelers seeking a quieter, history-focused stay away from the station bustle.

A mountain district on Nagano's western fringe centered on the ancient Togakushi Shrine complex and cedar-lined pilgrim trails; suits nature lovers and hikers wanting an alpine, forested base near the Japanese Alps.

transit.hours: Trains and buses generally run about 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; no late-night service.
transit.pay: IC cards (Suica/ICOCA compatible) are widely accepted on trains and most city buses; cash also works on buses.
transit.note: The Hokuriku Shinkansen makes Nagano an easy ~80-minute trip from Tokyo; local Nagaden trains and Alpico buses connect the station to Zenko-ji and outlying areas like Togakushi and the Snow Monkey Park.

air: Shinshu Matsumoto Airport (regional; most visitors arrive via Tokyo by Shinkansen)
bus: Highway buses to Tokyo, Matsumoto, and Kanazawa

airport.name: Shinshu Matsumoto Airport (FDA) — most visitors instead arrive via Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo (~80 min)

transit.m: Airport bus to Matsumoto then train to Nagano (~90 min total)
Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station (~80 min, unrelated to this airport)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can even cause confusion; excellent service is simply the standard, not something to reward with extra cash.

tagline: One of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities, layering Roman ruins, Ottoman-era Old Town, and a buzzing creative quarter.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered by law; use official yellow cabs with visible company names/rates on the door or book via the Bolt app to avoid overcharging, especially near the train station or airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and typically reaches an English-speaking operator who can connect police, fire, or ambulance.

hood_desc: Plovdiv's hilltop historic quarter of cobblestone lanes, National Revival-era mansions, and the 2nd-century Ancient Theatre still used for performances; best for travelers who want history underfoot.

The pedestrianized 'Creative District,' a maze of street art, indie galleries, craft coffee shops, and bars carved out of a once-derelict artisan quarter; suits younger travelers chasing Plovdiv's nightlife.

The pedestrian spine of Knyaz Alexander I Street linking Dzhumaya Square to the Singing Fountains, lined with shops, cafes, and Roman Stadium ruins; ideal for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
A quieter residential pocket nicknamed 'Little Paris' for its Vienna Secession and Baroque facades; appeals to travelers wanting a slower, local-feeling stay close to downtown.
A modern residential district with shopping malls and everyday local life away from the tourist core; suits budget travelers and longer stays wanting lower-cost lodging.
lodging: Best Western Plus Congress Hotel Plovdiv
Best Western Plus Congress Hotel Plovdiv

transit.hours: Buses generally run from about 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM; there is no dedicated night bus network.
transit.pay: Fares are paid via prepaid ticket, contactless card tap, or cash on board (around 1.60 BGN per ride, roughly 0.90 USD); there is no rechargeable citywide transit card as of 2026.
transit.note: Plovdiv has no metro or tram; city buses are the sole public transit mode, supplemented heavily by walking in the compact center, taxis, and ride-hailing apps.

air: Plovdiv International Airport (PDV) - limited seasonal/charter routes
Sofia Airport (SOF) - main gateway, about 2 hrs away by bus/train
train: Plovdiv Central Railway Station - lines to Sofia, Burgas, and Istanbul
bus: Yug (South) Bus Station - intercity coaches nationwide

transit.m: Connect via city bus from a nearby stop (limited direct service)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving around 10% at restaurants for good service is common but not expected.

tagline: Lombok's laid-back provincial capital and gateway to the Gili Islands and Mount Rinjani.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird taxis are metered and reliable; app-based ride-hailing (Gojek/Grab) operates but can face pickup restrictions near the airport and traditional taxi stands due to long-standing local driver protections.

emergency.note: 112 is a nationwide emergency number that can route to police, fire, or medical services, though an English-speaking operator is not guaranteed.

hood_desc: The historic port district with fading Dutch and Chinese colonial shopfronts, art galleries, and a lively Sunday street-art market along the coast; suits travelers wanting character and sunset views over the Lombok Strait.
The administrative and commercial heart of the city with government offices, malls, and the main square; convenient as a base with easy onward transport to the Gilis or Rinjani.
Lombok's busiest trading hub, home to the 18th-century Hindu-Balinese Pura Meru temple and the sprawling Cakranegara Market; good for street food and browsing local goods.
A craft neighborhood known for pearl and silver jewelry workshops where visitors can watch artisans at work and buy directly from makers; appeals to shoppers wanting authentic souvenirs.
A quieter, more residential area near the former Selaparang airport site; suits longer-stay visitors wanting a calmer, local-feeling base away from the busiest streets.

transit.hours: Angkot minivans and local buses generally run from about 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM; there is little to no public transit after dark.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the driver; angkot rides are flat-rate and inexpensive (roughly Rp 5,000-10,000), with no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.note: Mataram has no formal rapid transit; getting around relies on angkot minivans, motorbike taxis (ojek), Gojek/Grab, and rental scooters, which are also the most practical way to reach the Gilis ferry ports or Rinjani trailheads.

bus: Intercity buses toward Kayangan Port for Sumbawa connections
ferry: Bangsal/Teluk Nara harbor (boats to the Gili Islands)

transit.m: DAMRI airport shuttle bus to Mataram (~45 min)

tip.r: Tipping isn't traditionally expected; rounding up or leaving a small amount (Rp 10,000-20,000) for good service at restaurants and for drivers/guides is appreciated.

tagline: Golden Ring gem of 12th-century white-stone cathedrals on the Klyazma River.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked through the Yandex Go app with upfront pricing; foreign-issued Visa/Mastercard cards do not work in Russia, so cash (rubles) or a linked Yandex account is needed to pay.

emergency.note: 112 is the general emergency number and often the most reliable way to reach an operator who can transfer the call; English-speaking staff are not guaranteed.

hood_desc: The historic heart around Cathedral Square, home to the 12th-century Assumption Cathedral with frescoes by Andrei Rublev and the Vladimir-Suzdal Museum-Reserve; best for first-time visitors focused on the UNESCO sights.
A pedestrianized cobblestone street lined with the 12th-century Golden Gate, souvenir shops, and cozy cafes; suits travelers who want an easy, atmospheric stroll through old Vladimir.
The 19th-century covered market arcade of Bolshaya Moskovskaya Street, now filled with shops, bakeries, and street food stalls; good for browsing and casual dining.
A leafy stretch along the Klyazma River with an observation deck and water tower museum offering panoramic views; ideal for a relaxed walk after sightseeing.
A residential Soviet-era microdistrict away from the tourist center; suits budget travelers and longer stays wanting authentic local life at lower prices.

sys.n: Vladimir City Bus and Trolleybus Network

transit.hours: Buses and trolleybuses generally run from about 5:30 AM to 11:00 PM; there is no dedicated night service.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver or conductor (around 30-35 RUB per ride); some routes accept regional transit cards.
transit.note: Vladimir has no metro or tram; buses and trolleybuses cover the city, supplemented by fixed-route minibuses (marshrutky) and taxis.

air: No commercial airport in Vladimir; nearest major hub is Moscow (about 180 km away)
train: Vladimir railway station - direct trains/express service to Moscow (~2 hrs) and Nizhny Novgorod
bus: Intercity buses to Moscow, Suzdal, Ivanovo, Kostroma, and Nizhny Novgorod

transit.m: Train from Moscow (Kurgan/Kursky station area) to Vladimir (~2 hrs)
Intercity bus from Moscow to Vladimir (~3 hrs)

tip.r: Tipping isn't obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants in tourist areas is increasingly common but not expected.

tagline: Karst-peak river town on the Li and Yulong rivers, China's backpacker and rock-climbing capital near Guilin.

taxi.fareNote: Metered in town, but for trips to/from Guilin airport or countryside villages a flat negotiated fare is common; few drivers speak English.

emergency.note: 119 is for fire; English-speaking dispatch is limited, so having a hotel staffer or Mandarin speaker call is helpful.

hood_desc: Yangshuo's pedestrian tourist artery lined with bars, souvenir stalls, and guesthouses in restored Qing-era buildings; best for first-timers who want restaurants, nightlife, and Li River access within a five-minute walk.

The riverside promenade and park along the Li River just east of West Street, with cormorant-fishing demonstrations and sunset views; suits travelers who want a quieter base still close to the action.

A patchwork of rice paddies and limestone karsts along the Yulong River south of town, reached by bicycle or e-bike and dotted with farmhouse guesthouses and bamboo-raft docks; ideal for cyclists wanting rural scenery.

The area around Moon Hill's natural rock arch and the region's best rock-climbing routes, a short scooter ride from West Street; suits climbers, hikers, and those wanting mountain views over nightlife.
A slower-paced Ming and Qing-dynasty river town about 25 km north of Yangshuo, famous as the scenery on China's 20-yuan banknote; suits travelers seeking authentic village life away from the crowds.
lodging: Yangshuo West Street International Youth Hostel
Yangshuo West Street International Youth Hostel
Yangshuo West Street International Youth Hostel
Yangshuo West Street International Youth Hostel

transit.hours: Local buses and shuttles typically run roughly 6:30 AM to 9:30 PM; no late-night public transit.
transit.pay: Cash or mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat Pay) on buses; no rechargeable transit card system in Yangshuo.
transit.note: Yangshuo itself has no metro or extensive city bus network; most visitors get around by bicycle, e-bike, taxi, or bamboo raft, with buses and a high-speed rail station connecting to Guilin (about an hour away).

ferry: Li River cruise boats and bamboo rafts

car.idp: Not valid; a Chinese driving license is required to drive, so self-drive rental is uncommon for foreign visitors

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Guilin, then bus/train transfer to Yangshuo (~2.5 hrs total)
Private taxi/car direct to Yangshuo (75-90 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary and can even cause confusion; upscale hotels or tour groups may add a service charge instead.

tagline: Chile's 'Garden City' of Pacific beaches, Belle Époque palaces, and the famous international song festival.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis (taxi básico) use meters by law; colectivos (shared taxis) run fixed routes for a flat, low fare and are common for short local hops.

emergency.note: 132 is for fire (Bomberos); 133 (Carabineros) is the most commonly used number for general emergencies.

hood_desc: The walkable downtown core around Plaza Vergara and the Flower Clock, close to Avenida Valparaíso's shops, the casino, and the Marga Marga estuary; best for first-timers who want everything within walking distance.
Viña del Mar's most popular beach neighborhood to the north, packed with high-rise apartments, beach clubs, and summer nightlife; suits travelers prioritizing beach time and a lively scene.
A hillside residential district overlooking the coast, home to the president's summer residence and quiet tree-lined streets; suits travelers wanting calm and sea views away from the crowds.
The park and open-air amphitheater that hosts the famous Viña del Mar International Song Festival every February, alongside the Palacio Vergara and botanical gardens; suits culture-focused visitors.
A quieter southern beach and residential area near the naval base and Museo Fonck, less crowded than Reñaca; suits travelers wanting a relaxed, local beach experience.
lodging: Diego de Almagro Viña del Mar

transit.hours: Merval trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; local buses run similar hours with reduced late-night frequency.
transit.pay: Rechargeable 'Tarjeta Multivía' contactless card for Merval; buses are typically paid in cash or with the same card.
transit.note: The Merval commuter rail directly connects Viña del Mar with Valparaíso and inland Quilpué, Villa Alemana, and Limache; colectivos supplement buses on fixed routes.

air: Nearest major gateway: Comodoro Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL), Santiago
train: Merval commuter rail to Valparaíso and Limache
bus: Pullman Bus (intercity to Santiago and beyond)

airport.name: Comodoro Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL), Santiago

transit.m: Turbus/Pullman direct bus SCL-Viña del Mar (~1.5-2 hrs)

tip.r: A 10% tip (propina) is commonly added to restaurant bills, sometimes suggested automatically on the receipt; appreciated but not legally obligatory.

tagline: The Netherlands' cycling-friendly canal city, crowned by the Dom Tower and its historic university.

taxi.color: no fixed color; licensed cabs carry blue 'TX' plates
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with government-regulated maximum rates; street hailing is uncommon — phone, app, or taxi ranks are standard, and Uber/Bolt operate alongside local taxis.

emergency.note: 112 connects to police, fire, and ambulance nationwide and is answered in English as well as Dutch.

hood_desc: The historic core around the Dom Tower and the sunken Oudegracht canal with its unique wharf cellars turned into cafes and restaurants; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.

A multicultural neighborhood west of the center built around the Kanaalstraat market, known for diverse eateries, independent shops, and a laid-back, creative vibe; suits budget-conscious and adventurous eaters.

A leafy, upscale residential area east of downtown centered on its namesake English-style park, popular with families and students; suits travelers wanting quiet, green surroundings close to the center.

The modern square and nightlife hub around the Neude and Vredenburg, home to the TivoliVredenburg concert hall and Hoog Catharijne shopping center next to Utrecht Centraal; suits travelers who want music, bars, and shopping.

A large modern district on Utrecht's western edge with contemporary architecture, shopping malls, and green space, connected to the center by tram and bus; suits travelers wanting new-build comfort over historic charm.

transit.hours: Buses and trams run roughly 6:00 AM to midnight, with a limited night bus network on weekends.
transit.pay: OV-chipkaart (tap in/tap out) or contactless bank/credit card are standard on all buses, trams, and trains; single paper tickets are pricier and less common.
transit.note: Utrecht Centraal is the Netherlands' busiest train station; cycling is the dominant way locals get around, with an extensive bike-lane network and the world's largest bicycle parking garage at the station.

train: NS Intercity and Sprinter trains via Utrecht Centraal

car.idp: Not required for EU/EEA licenses; recommended for others

transit.m: Direct NS train Schiphol-Utrecht Centraal (~30 min, several per hour)

tip.r: Service is included in menu prices by law; rounding up the bill or adding 5-10% for good service at sit-down restaurants is a nice gesture but not expected.
